items.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: At that time, a gentleman called Mr. Morris Levy at Roulette. I told him... He brought me in and he said, “Mr. Palmieri, what did you record for me?”

ctx.x: Because I was accused of being a Communist by the first Cubans that came from Cuba. The CIA and FBI went to see my record company. At that time, a gentleman called Mr. Morris Levy at Roulette. I told him... He brought me in and he said, “Mr. Palmieri, what did you record for me? What did you do this time?” “I told him it’s a rhythm called Mozambique, that it’s coming out of Cuba. The fighting in Angola, I’ve got nothing to do with that, but it’s a rhythmical pattern that we play, and it’s the old conga, Mr.…
